Users message the agent with trip ideas like ski escapes or dinner plans; it researches, personalizes options, books flights and hotels via partners, and monitors prices or disruptions. The private beta is open now on web and text, with plans to expand the team and supplier network for dining and experiences.

news.summary: Hugging Face launched Qwen3.8-27B-pi-adapted, a small LoRA adapter trained with reinforcement learning to enhance Alibaba's Qwen3.8-27B model for the pi coding agent. It jumps SWE-bench Pro pass@1 from 29.4% to 62.7% and Terminal-Bench 2.1 from 39.5% to 55.8%, while using 55-62% fewer tool calls to speed up tasks. Part of the 'harness adapters' initiative, the 640 MB adapter works alongside base model weights, with open files for easy testing—developers praise the efficiency for local workflows, though some note results tie to specific pi conditions.

news.hook: Output Labs unveiled Bonbon, a biology AI that spots hidden molecular links on its own—and it just delivered a 61.5% hit rate in real lab tests, dwarfing traditional methods.
news.name: Bonbon AI Model Transforms Drug Discovery with Lab-Validated Success
news.summary: The 1.6-billion-parameter model, trained on 3.2 trillion protein-ligand tokens, predicts drug mechanisms, binding sites, and engagement types without structural data or fine-tuning. In external wet-lab tests across nine disease targets, Bonbon-prioritized molecules succeeded at a 61.5% rate—versus 0.1% for standard screening—with many structurally novel and effective on untrained targets. Team members and investors praised its 50,000x speed boost and rigorous approach, earning it a top NeurIPS 2026 presentation slot.

This brings total funding to $605 million since their seed round less than 18 months ago. Their Eno robot, with human-like dexterous hands for tasks like wire routing and packaging, uses sensor gloves, a custom AI model, and simulator to tackle manufacturing, logistics, and lab work. Plans call for U.S. mass production and deployments in 2027.

news.hook: Cancer isn't just one rogue cell—it's a bustling neighborhood of interacting cells. CellType and Inventia just launched a benchmark to test if AI can predict what happens when those neighbors change.
news.name: CellType and Inventia Launch Tumor Context AI Benchmark for Cancer
news.summary: Tumor Context, built on the BioSimBench platform, uses real 3D tumor models from Inventia's RASTRUM system to challenge AI models on forecasting gene expression shifts in varied cellular environments. Early tests show top AI models hitting a 0.76 correlation with lab results, compared to 0.97 from repeated experiments, highlighting clear room for improvement. The benchmark helps AI labs train better models and drug developers study specific tumors, grounded in actual biology from controlled lab setups. Observers praise it as a practical step toward AI understanding complex cancer systems.

Developers suggest fixes like AI summaries, quizzes before merging, and small changes for human review. The discussion weighs AI's speed against the need for lasting understanding and maintenance.

news.hook: Imagine a single nuclear blast high above Earth knocking out nearly all satellites in low orbit within a week. That's the stark warning from a new study drawing real lessons from a 1962 U.S. test.
news.name: Study Warns One Orbital Nuclear Blast Could Wipe Out Most LEO Satellites
news.summary: Researchers simulated a 1-megaton explosion at 500 kilometers over the South Atlantic Anomaly, where an X-ray flash and trapped electrons would form a damaging radiation belt. The model predicts 98 percent of low-Earth orbit satellites failing in seven days, even with triple radiation shielding, within two weeks. It factors in lost maneuverability causing 20 collisions over two years, plus years of lingering radiation, hitting modern networks like Starlink hard and disrupting global navigation, communications, and weather systems.

news.hook: Imagine handing off a half-done coding task to an AI teammate—can it pick up the threads, ask the right questions, and deliver a working patch? A new benchmark tests exactly that in simulated workplaces.
news.name: SWE-CoWork Benchmark Reveals AI Coding Agents' Teamwork Struggles
news.summary: TokenWave.AI launched SWE-CoWork, a realistic test using 101 real open-source tasks across 11 languages where AI agents must query simulated teammates, search docs, write code, and pass hidden checks in one run. Top models like Claude-Opus-5.5 hit 63.84% on partial tests but only 6.93% full completion, with GPT-6 Astra close behind at 7.92%. Experts note agents falter on handoffs and revisions despite having info, as 82% of requirements come from 'colleagues,' showing they still need human oversight for full engineering workflows. The public benchmark, released November 15 on arXiv, traces failures to highlight gaps in long tasks.
